The conflict ended in a treaty ceding the Indus Valley and adjoining regions to the Mauryas in exchange for 500 war elephants and sealed by a marriage alliance.

name: Battle of Ilipa
locations: Ilipa, near modern Alcalá del Río, Hispania Baetica (Spain)
description: Scipio Africanus outmaneuvered a larger Carthaginian army under Hasdrubal Gisco and Mago in southern Spain through a sophisticated double-envelopment. The victory effectively ended Carthaginian power in the Iberian Peninsula.

description: France and Spain competed for control of Milan and Naples, with Spain ultimately establishing dominance in southern Italy. This war consolidated Spanish power in the Mediterranean.

name: Venetian-Ottoman War
description: The Ottoman Navy defeated Venice in several naval engagements, establishing Ottoman naval dominance in the Mediterranean. Venice lost key territories including Greek possessions.

name: American Indian Wars
description: Three centuries of conflict between European colonists and Native American peoples resulted in the near-total displacement of Native Americans. These wars transformed North American demographics and geography.

name: Aztec Tributary Uprisings
description: Periodic rebellions by tributary states against Aztec dominance. These revolts weakened empire cohesion and demonstrated resentment of Aztec rule.

name: Battle of Calicut
partOf: Early Portuguese Colonial Wars in Asia
description: Battle of Calicut (1790), part of the 3rd British-Mysore War. United Kingdom defeated Mysore.

name: Battle of Hemmingstedt
description: Battle of Hemmingstedt (1500), part of the Wars of the Kalmar Union. Holstein farmers defeated Denmark, North German nobles, German mercenaries.

name: Battle of Jabani
description: Battle of Jabani (1500), part of the Persian-Turcoman Wars. Ardabil defeated Azerbaijan.

name: Battle of Novara
description: Battle of Novara (1500), part of the 1st Italian War of Independence. Austria defeated Piedmont, Polish Volunteers.

name: Battle of Vedrosha
description: Battle of Vedrosha (1500), part of the 1st Muscovite-Lithuanian War. Moscow defeated Lithuania.

name: Benin-Yoruba Conflicts
description: Territorial and commercial conflicts between Benin and neighboring Yoruba city-states.

name: Benin–Itsekiri Wars
description: Wars between Benin and its breakaway Itsekiri kingdom of Warri.

name: Brazilian Indigenous Resistance to Portuguese
description: Centuries-long indigenous resistance to Portuguese colonial expansion. Tupi, Guaraní, and other groups resisted Portuguese settlement and enslavement.

name: Bruneian conquest of Manila
description: Brunei extended its empire over Manila Bay in the late 15th century.

name: Burmese-Mon Wars
description: Burmese forces gradually conquered and absorbed the Mon Kingdom, extending Burmese rule over lower Burma. This conquest created the modern extent of Burmese territory.

name: Cambodian-Thai Wars
description: Conflicts between Cambodia and Siam resulted in Thai expansion and Cambodian contraction, reducing Cambodia to a vassal state. These wars reshaped Southeast Asian power dynamics.

name: French-Spanish Colonial Wars
description: Centuries of conflict between France and Spain over colonial territories in North America and the Caribbean resulted in gradual French expansion. The conflicts concluded with British dominance in North America.

name: Funj Conquest of Alodia
description: Funj founder Amara Dunqas's destruction of the Christian Nubian kingdom of Alodia and foundation of the Sennar Sultanate.

name: Hausa-Fulani Conflicts
description: Territorial and cultural conflicts between Hausa city-states and Fulani pastoralists.

name: Incan Provincial Revolts
description: Various provincial uprisings against Inca imperial rule in the decades before Spanish conquest. Demonstrated imperial vulnerability to internal revolt.

name: Ottoman-Circassian Wars
description: Ottoman conflicts with Caucasian peoples including Circassians resulted in massive depopulation and displacement. Ottoman control of the Caucasus remained contested against local resistance.

name: Ottoman-Georgian Wars
description: Georgian kingdoms faced pressure from both Ottoman and Persian powers, gradually coming under Ottoman and Russian influence. Georgia became a contested borderland between empires.

name: Ottoman-Hungarian Wars
description: A century of warfare between the Ottomans and Hungary resulted in Ottoman conquest of much of Hungary. These conflicts lasted until the Treaty of Zsitvatorok in 1606.

name: Polish-Ottoman Conflicts
description: Centuries of conflicts between Poland-Lithuania and the Ottoman Empire over territorial control of Eastern Europe and the Balkans resulted in Ottoman expansion to Europe. Poland ultimately declined as Ottoman power waned.

name: Portuguese Conquest of Brazil
description: Portuguese conquistadors and settlers gradually conquered Brazil from indigenous peoples and competing European powers, establishing Portugal's largest and most valuable colony. The conquest devastated indigenous populations through warfare and disease.

name: Portuguese Expansion in Africa
description: Portuguese explorers and traders established coastal fortresses and trading posts across Africa, beginning European colonization of the continent. Portuguese naval superiority allowed them to dominate African coastal trade for two centuries.

name: Powhatan-Monacan Wars
description: Territorial conflicts between the powerful Powhatan Confederacy and the Monacan peoples of the Virginia Piedmont. Powhatan dominance was established by the time of European settlement.

name: Russian-Polish Conflicts
description: Centuries of conflicts between Russia and Poland-Lithuania over Eastern Europe resulted in Polish decline and Russian expansion. Russia ultimately partitioned Poland by 1795.

name: Songhai Conquest of Air
description: Askia Muhammad's conquest of Agadez and the Aïr massif.

name: Spanish Expansion in North Africa
description: Spanish forces conquered several North African coastal enclaves and fought Ottoman and Moroccan forces for regional dominance. Spanish control remained limited to small coastal areas.

name: Vietnamese Expansion South - Nam Vu
description: Vietnamese states gradually conquered the Kingdom of Champa and expanded southward into the Mekong Delta, creating modern Vietnam's territorial extent. This expansion displaced numerous Southeast Asian populations and established Vietnamese dominance in Indochina.

name: Battle of Helmed
description: Battle of Helmed (1501), part of the 1st Muscovite-Lithuanian War. Russia defeated Livonian Order.

name: Battle of Mstislavl
description: Battle of Mstislavl (1501), part of the 1st Muscovite Lithuanian War. Moscow defeated Lithuana, Poland.

name: Battle of Sar-i-Pul
description: Battle of Sar-i-Pul (1501), part of the Mughal-Uzbek War. Uzbekistan defeated Mughal Empire.

name: Battle of Seritsa
description: Battle of Seritsa (1501), part of the 1st Muscovite-Lithuanian War. Lithuanian-Polish Commonwealth, Livonian Order defeated Russia.

name: Battle of Sharur
description: Battle of Sharur (1501), part of the Persian-Turkoman Wars. Ardibil defeated White Sheep Turks.

name: Safavid Empire Formation
description: The Safavid Dynasty conquered Persia, establishing Shia Islam as the state religion and creating a major Islamic empire. The Safavids rivaled the Ottomans for centuries as the dominant Middle Eastern power.

name: Battle of Barletta
description: Battle of Barletta (1502), part of the Italian War of Louis XII. Spain defeated France, Swiss Mercenaries.

name: Battle of Lake Smolino
description: Battle of Lake Smolino (1502), part of the 1st Muscovite Lithuanian War.

name: Battle of Smolensk
description: Battle of Smolensk (1943), part of the World War II. USSR defeated Germany.

name: Battle of Akhsikath
description: Battle of Akhsikath (1503), part of the Mughal-Uzbek Wars. Uzbeks defeated Mughal Empire.

name: Battle of Cerignola
description: On 28 April 1503 a Spanish army under Gonzalo Fernandez de Cordoba defeated a French force in the Kingdom of Naples, generally regarded as the first major European battle won by gunpowder small arms (arquebuses behind entrenchments).

name: Battle of Zanzibar
partOf: Later Portuguese Wars in East Africa
description: Battle of Zanzibar (1652), part of the Later Portuguese Wars in East Africa. Oman defeated Portugal.

name: Battle of Kabul
description: Battle of Kabul (1996), part of the Afghan Civil War. Taliban defeated Ahmed Shah Masud, Gulbudin Hekmatyar. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Knockdoe
description: Battle of Knockdoe (1504), part of the Irish Baron's War. England, Kildare defeated Munster.

name: Funj Conquest of Soba
description: Around 1504-05 the Funj under Amara Dunqas captured Soba, capital of the Christian Nubian kingdom of Alodia, founding the Funj Sultanate of Sennar that dominated the central Nile for three centuries.

name: Battle of Mers el Kebir
partOf: Spanish Colonial War in North Africa
description: Battle of Mers el Kebir (1940), part of the World War II. United Kingdom defeated France.

name: Portuguese Conquest of Mozambique
description: Portuguese forces conquered Mozambique from Arab traders and Swahili states, establishing Portuguese control of the southeastern African coast. Portuguese rule lasted until the 20th century.

name: Portuguese Expansion in India
description: Portuguese forces conquered Goa and other Indian ports, establishing a Portuguese maritime empire in the Indian Ocean. Portuguese dominance of Indian Ocean trade lasted until challenged by the Dutch and British.

name: Portuguese sack of Kilwa (1505)
description: Almeida built the Gereza fort and installed a Portuguese puppet sultan at Kilwa, beginning Lusitanian rule on the Swahili coast.

name: Portuguese sack of Mombasa (1505)
description: Francisco de Almeida's fleet stormed and burned Mombasa on the first Portuguese reconnaissance of the Swahili coast.

name: Portuguese-Swahili Conflicts
description: Conflicts over control of East African trade routes between Portuguese colonizers and Swahili traders.

name: Battle of Cochin
partOf: Early Portuguese Colonial Wars in Asia
description: Battle of Cochin (1506), part of the Early Portuguese Colonial Wars in Asia. Portugal defeated Calicut.

name: Battle of Kleck
description: Battle of Kleck (1506), part of the Polish Crimean Tatar Wars. Poland defeated Crimean Tatars.

name: Kongo Civil War of 1506
description: Succession war in which the Christian prince Mvemba a Nzinga (Afonso I) defeated his pagan half-brother Mpanzu a Kitima at the Battle of Mbanza Kongo, securing the throne and the Portuguese alliance.

name: Kongo-Portuguese Conflicts
description: Long conflict between Portuguese colonial ambitions and the Kingdom of Kongo. See per-war entries.

name: Battle of Maruchak
description: Battle of Maruchak (1507), part of the Mughal-Uzbek Wars. Uzbekistan defeated Mughal Empire.

name: Battle of Muscat
partOf: Later Portuguese Colonial Wars in Arabia
description: Battle of Muscat (1650), part of the Later Portuguese Colonial Wars in Arabia. Oman defeated Portugal.

name: Battle of Cadore
description: Battle of Cadore (1508), part of the War of the League of Cambrai. Venice defeated Germany, France, Spain, Papal States.

name: Battle of Chaul
partOf: Early Portuguese Colonial Wars in Asia
description: Battle of Chaul (1508), part of the Early Portuguese Colonial Wars in Asia. Egypt, Gujarat defeated Portugal.

name: Battle of Kandahar
description: Battle of Kandahar (2001), part of the Afghanistan War. United States, United Kingdom, Northern Alliance defeated Taliban.

name: War of the League of Cambrai
Battle of Agnadello
description: Battle of Agnadello (1509), part of the War of the League of Cambrai. France defeated Venice.

name: Battle of Diu
partOf: Early Portuguese Colonial Wars in Asia
description: Battle of Diu (1546), part of the Portuguese Colonial Wars in Asia. Portugal defeated Gujarat.

name: Battle of Padua
description: Battle of Padua (1509), part of the War of the League of Cambrai. Holy Roman Empire, Papal States defeated Venice.

name: Portuguese-Ottoman Conflicts in Indian Ocean
description: Portuguese naval forces competed with Ottoman and Arab powers for control of Indian Ocean trade routes, establishing Portuguese naval dominance. Though eventually challenged by other European powers, Portugal maintained regional influence for centuries.

name: Spanish Conquest of Oran
description: Cardinal Cisneros's expedition capturing Oran, part of the Spanish offensive into the Maghreb after the fall of Granada.

name: Battle of Bougie
partOf: Spanish Colonial Wars in North Africa
description: Battle of Bougie (1671), part of the Corsair Wars. England defeated Algiers.

name: Battle of Goa
partOf: Early Portuguese Colonial Wars in Asia
description: Battle of Goa (1604), part of the Dutch-Portuguese Colonial Wars. Netherlands defeated Portugal.

name: Battle of Los Gelves
partOf: Spanish Colonial Wars in North Africa
description: Battle of Los Gelves (1510), part of the Spanish Colonial Wars in North Africa. Moors defeated Spain.

name: Battle of Tripoli, Libya
partOf: Spanish Colonial Wars in North Africa
description: Battle of Tripoli, Libya (1911), part of the Italo-Turkish War. Italy defeated Ottoman Empire.

name: Portuguese Conquest of Goa
description: Portuguese forces under Afonso de Albuquerque conquered the strategic port city of Goa, establishing a major Portuguese colonial center in India. Goa served as the capital of Portuguese India for centuries.

name: Toungoo Dynasty Expansion
description: Toungoo's expansion creating Burmese hegemony.

name: Battle of Algiers
partOf: Spanish Colonial Wars in North Africa
description: Battle of Algiers (1956), part of the Algerian War. France defeated FLN.

name: Battle of Casalechio
description: Battle of Casalechio (1511), part of the War of the Holy League. France defeated Papal States.

name: Battle of Goodwin Sands
description: Battle of Goodwin Sands (1652), part of the 1st Dutch War. England defeated Netherlands.

name: Battle of Kayseri
description: Battle of Kayseri (1624), part of the Anatolian Rebellion. Ottoman Empire defeated Ottoman Governor of Anatolia.

name: Battle of Mirandola
description: Battle of Mirandola (1511), part of the War of the Holy League. Papal States, Venice defeated France.

name: Battle of Pul-i-Sanghin
description: Battle of Pul-i-Sanghin (1511), part of the Mughal-Uzbek Wars. Mughal Empire defeated Uzbekistan.

name: Capture of Malacca (1511)
description: Afonso de Albuquerque seized Malacca, beginning European naval primacy in Southeast Asia.

name: Battle of Ghujduwan
description: Battle of Ghujduwan (1512), part of the Mughal-Uzbek Wars. Uzbekistan defeated Persia, Mughal Empire.

name: Battle of Kul-i-Malik
description: Battle of Kul-i-Malik (1512), part of the Mughal-Uzbek Wars. Uzbekistan defeated Mughal Empire.

name: Portuguese Conquest of the Spice Islands
description: Portuguese traders and soldiers fought to monopolize spice trade in the Moluccas, establishing fortified trading posts before being displaced by the Dutch. The Moluccas became the source of Europe's spice wealth.

name: Portuguese Spice Wars in Moluccas
description: Portuguese traders and soldiers fought to monopolize the spice trade in the Moluccas, establishing fortified trading posts. Portuguese control gradually declined as the Dutch and British challenged their dominance.

name: Battle of Aden
description: Battle of Aden (1994), part of the Yemeni Civil Wars. Yemen defeated Democratic Republic of Yemen.

name: Battle of Broomhouse
description: Battle of Broomhouse (1513), part of the Anglo-Scottish Border Wars. England defeated Scotland.

name: Battle of Flodden
description: The English victory against Scotland that killed King James IV and many Scottish nobles.

name: Battle of Vicenza
description: Battle of Vicenza (1848), part of the 1st Italian War of Independence. Austria defeated Sardinia.

name: Battle of Chaldiran
description: Ottoman forces decisively defeated the Safavid Empire, establishing Ottoman control over Mesopotamia and much of the Caucasus. This battle marked the beginning of centuries of Ottoman-Persian rivalry.

name: Battle of Orsha
description: Battle of Orsha (1514), part of the 2nd Muscovite- Lithuanian War. Poland defeated Russia.

name: Battle of Temesvar
description: Battle of Temesvar (1849), part of the Hungarian Revolutionary War. Austria, Russia defeated Hungarian Rebels.

name: Ottoman-Safavid War
description: A prolonged conflict saw Ottoman and Safavid forces struggle for control of Iraq and the Caucasus, with both empires suffering significant losses. The war resulted in Ottoman recovery of Baghdad and Mesopotamian territories.

name: Battle of Hormuz
description: Battle of Hormuz (1622), part of the Anglo-Portuguese Colonial Wars. England, Safavid Persia defeated Portugal.

name: Battle of Kondavidu
description: Battle of Kondavidu (1563), part of the War of the Deccan Sultanate. Bijapur, Vijayanagar defeated Golconda, Ahmadnagar.

name: Battle of Marignano
description: Fought 13-14 September 1515 near Melegnano (16 km SE of Milan), the newly crowned Francis I of France decisively defeated the Swiss pikemen, ending the legend of Swiss invincibility and securing the Duchy of Milan.

name: Battle of Turna Dag
description: Battle of Turna Dag (1515), part of the Turko-Persian War in Anatolia. Ottoman Empire defeated Principality of Dulgadir.

name: Kebbi–Songhai War
description: Kanta Kotal's revolt against Askia Muhammad founded the kingdom of Kebbi and broke Songhai control of Hausaland's western marches.

name: Battle of Marj Dabik
description: Battle of Marj Dabik (1516), part of the Ottoman-Mamluk War. Ottoman Empire defeated Mamluk Egypt.

name: Battle of Yaunis Khan
description: Battle of Yaunis Khan (1516), part of the Ottoman-Mamluk War. Ottoman Empire defeated Mamluks.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Algiers
description: Ottoman forces took control of Algiers, establishing Ottoman dominance over the Barbary States of North Africa. Algiers became a major Ottoman naval base for the next 300 years.

name: Ottoman Conquest of North Africa
description: Ottoman forces and Barbary corsairs conquered North African territories from Spain and established Ottoman dominance. The Barbary States became autonomous Ottoman provinces.

name: Battle of Champoton
description: Battle of Champoton (1517), part of the Spanish Conquest of Yucatan. Mayans defeated Spain.

name: Fall of Majapahit
description: Demak's destruction of the last Majapahit court at Daha around 1527.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Mecca and Medina
description: Ottoman forces conquered the Islamic holy cities of Mecca and Medina from the Mamluks, establishing Ottoman control and prestige. The Ottomans became recognized as protectors of Islam.

name: Battle of Brannkyrka
description: Battle of Brannkyrka (1518), part of the Wars of the Kalmar Union. Sweden defeated Denmark.

name: Johor–Portuguese wars
description: Century-long Johor effort to reclaim Malacca from Portugal.

name: Battle of Ceutla
description: Battle of Ceutla (1519), part of the Spanish Conquest of Mexico. Spain defeated Maya.

name: Battle of Cholula
description: Battle of Cholula (1519), part of the Spanish Conquest of Mexico. Spain, Tlaxcans defeated Cholula.

name: Battle of Cintla
description: In March 1519, Hernan Cortes's small expedition defeated the Chontal Maya of Potonchan on the plain of Cintla in Tabasco, the first pitched battle of his march on the Aztec Empire; the defeated lords gave Cortes gifts including the interpreter Malinche.

name: Battle of Potonchan
description: Battle of Potonchan (1519), part of the Spanish Conquest of Mexico. Spain defeated Chontal Mayans.

name: Battle of Tlaxcala
description: Battle of Tlaxcala (1519), part of the Spanish Conquest of Mexico. Spain defeated Tlaxcala, Otomi.

name: Spanish Conquest of Mexico
description: Hernán Cortés led a relatively small Spanish force that conquered the massive Aztec Empire, largely through exploitation of indigenous rivalries and disease. This conquest established Spanish control over Mesoamerica and resulted in catastrophic population decline.

name: Spanish Conquest of the Aztec Empire
description: Hernán Cortés led Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire, resulting in the fall of Tenochtitlan and Spanish dominion over Mexico.

name: Battle of Bogesund
description: Battle of Bogesund (1520), part of the Wars of the Kalmar Union. Denmark defeated Sweden.

name: Battle of Cempoala
description: Battle of Cempoala (1520), part of the Spanish Conquest of Mexico. Hernan Cortes defeated Panfilo de Narvaez.

name: Battle of Otumba
description: On 7 July 1520, days after the disastrous Spanish retreat from Tenochtitlan (La Noche Triste), Hernan Cortes's battered force and Tlaxcalan allies defeated a large Aztec army on the plain near Otumba, allowing Cortes to regroup and eventually return to besiege the Aztec capital.

name: Battle of Raichur
description: In 1520 Krishnadevaraya's Vijayanagara army defeated the Bijapur Sultanate at Raichur, capturing the contested Doab fortress and marking the high point of Vijayanagara military power in the Deccan.

name: Portuguese Conquest of East Timor
description: Portuguese explorers and traders gradually conquered East Timor through military campaigns and diplomacy, establishing Portuguese colonial control. Portuguese rule lasted until the 20th century.

name: Spanish Conquest of Northern Mexico
description: Spanish expansion into northern Mexico against fierce indigenous resistance. Slow and difficult conquest of nomadic and semi-nomadic peoples.

name: Battle of Bahrain
partOf: Later Portuguese Colonial Wars in Arabia
description: Battle of Bahrain (1602), part of the Later Portuguese Colonial Wars in Arabia. Persia defeated Portugal.

name: Battle of Esquiroz
description: Battle of Esquiroz (1521), part of the 1st Habsburg-Valois War. Habsburg Empire defeated France.

name: Battle of Mactan
description: Lapulapu's warriors killed Magellan in 1521.

name: Battle of Villalar
description: Battle of Villalar (1521), part of the Comuneros Uprising. Spain defeated Comuneros Rebels. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Italian Wars - Franco-Spanish Conflicts
description: A series of devastating wars between France and the Spanish-controlled Holy Roman Empire over control of Italian territories and European hegemony. These conflicts transformed European diplomacy and military tactics.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Belgrade
description: Ottoman forces captured Belgrade from Hungary, establishing Ottoman control of the Danube region. This conquest opened the way for further Ottoman advances into Central Europe.

name: Battle of Bicocca
description: Battle of Bicocca (1522), part of the Habsburg-Valois War. Spain defeated France, Swiss Mercenaries.

name: Battle of Genoa
description: Battle of Genoa (1800), part of the French Revolutionary War (2nd Coalition). United Kingdom, Austria defeated France.

name: Oromo migrations
description: Successive luba-led Oromo gadaa expansions described in Bahrey's Zenahu la Galla, transforming the political geography of the Horn after the Gragn wars.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Rhodes
description: Ottoman forces conquered Rhodes from the Knights Hospitaller, extending Ottoman dominance in the Mediterranean. This victory eliminated a major Christian stronghold in the Eastern Mediterranean.

name: Battle of Landstuhl
description: Battle of Landstuhl (1523), part of the German Knights War. Hesse, the Palatinate, Archbishopric of Trier defeated Franconian Knights.

name: Spanish conquest of Chiapas
description: A protracted Spanish campaign beginning in 1523 to subdue the highland and lowland Maya groups of Chiapas, including the resistant Lacandon, which dragged on into the late 17th century before colonial control was consolidated.

name: Battle of Marseilles
description: Battle of Marseilles (1944), part of the World War II. France defeated Germany.

name: Battle of Quetzaltenango
description: Battle of Quetzaltenango (1524), part of the Spanish Conquest of Guatemala. Spain defeated Quiche.

name: Battle of Rebecco
description: Battle of Rebecco (1524), part of the 1st Habsburg-Valois War. Spain defeated France.

name: Battle of Sesia
description: Battle of Sesia (1524), part of the 1st Habsburg Valois War. Habsburg Empire defeated France.

name: Battle of Ututlan
description: Battle of Ututlan (1524), part of the Spanish Conquest of Guatemala. Spain, Cakchiquel Indians defeated Quiche.

name: Battle of Vilcaconga
description: Battle of Vilcaconga (1524), part of the Spanish Conquest of Peru. Spain defeated Inca Empire.

name: German Peasants' War
description: A massive peasant uprising against nobility and clergy was brutally crushed, killing hundreds of thousands. Though inspired by Lutheran reformation ideas, the movement was ultimately crushed by nobles and princes.

name: Spanish Conquest of Guatemala
description: Spanish conquest of Guatemala led by Pedro de Alvarado. Vicious campaigns against K'iche' and other Maya kingdoms, with Spanish aided by indigenous allies.

name: Spanish conquest of Honduras
description: The Spanish conquest of Honduras (1524-1539) involved rival conquistador factions and fierce indigenous resistance, culminating in the Lenca uprising led by the chief Lempira before colonial control was established.

name: Battle of Boblingen
description: Battle of Boblingen (1525), part of the Peasants War. German Lords defeated German peasants. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Frankenhausen
description: Battle of Frankenhausen (1525), part of the German Peasants War. Saxony, Hesse defeated German peasant rebels.

name: Battle of Frauenberg
description: Battle of Frauenberg (1525), part of the German Peasant's War. Wurzburg and Franconia defeated German peasant rebels.

name: Battle of Ingolstadt
description: Battle of Ingolstadt (1525), part of the German Peasants War. Electorate of Palatine defeated German peasants.

name: Battle of Kempten
description: Battle of Kempten (1525), part of the German Peasants War. German aristocrats defeated German peasants. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Konigshofen
description: Battle of Konigshofen (1525), part of the German Peasant's War. Georg Truchsess von Waldburg defeated Rebel Peasants.

name: Battle of Leipheim
description: Battle of Leipheim (1525), part of the German Peasants War. Catholic Army defeated German Peasant Rebels. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Pavia
description: The Spanish victory over France that captured King Francis I and shifted the balance in Italian conflicts.

name: Battle of Zabern
description: Battle of Zabern (1525), part of the German Peasants' War. Duke Antoine of Lorraine defeated German peasant rebels. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Linlithgow Bridge
description: Battle of Linlithgow Bridge (1526), part of the Scottish Royalist War. the Earl of Arran defeated the Earl of Lennox.

name: Battle of Melrose
description: Battle of Melrose (1526), part of the Scottish Royalist War. Earl Archibald of Douglas defeated Sir Walter Scott of Bucleuch.

name: Battle of Mohács
description: Ottoman Sultan Suleiman defeated Hungarian forces, beginning Ottoman conquest of Hungary and establishing Ottoman dominance in the Balkans. This victory marked the beginning of Ottoman expansion into Central Europe.

name: Battle of Panipat
description: Battle of Panipat (1556), part of the Mughal Conquest of Northern India. Mughal Empire defeated Afghanistan, Hindus.

name: Battle of Peterwardein
description: Battle of Peterwardein (1716), part of the Austro-Turkish War. Habsburg Empire defeated Ottoman Empire.

name: Battle of Schladming
description: Battle of Schladming (1526), part of the German Peasants War. Styrian Peasants defeated Bohemian Mercenaries. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Sunda Kelapa
description: Fatahillah's 1527 victory renamed Sunda Kelapa to Jayakarta.

name: Mughal Expansion in India
description: The Mughal Empire expanded across much of India under Akbar and his successors, creating one of history's largest and wealthiest empires. Mughal rule transformed Indian culture, administration, and religion for centuries.

name: War of the League of Cognac
Battle of Ava
description: Battle of Ava (1752), part of the Burmese Civil War. Mon defeated Toungoo. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Khanua
description: Battle of Khanua (1527), part of the Mughal Conquest of Northern India. Mughal Empire defeated Mewar.

name: Battle of Khanwa
description: On 16 March 1527 Babur's Mughal army defeated the Rajput confederacy under Rana Sanga of Mewar near Khanwa (west of Agra), using gunpowder and field fortifications to consolidate Mughal power in northern India after Panipat.

name: Battle of Tokay
description: Battle of Tokay (1527), part of the Turkish-Habsburg War. Habsburg Empire defeated Ottoman Empire, Transylvania.

name: Spanish Conquest of Yucatán
description: Protracted Spanish conquest of Yucatán under Francisco de Montejo. Maya resistance was fierce and prolonged, with final subjugation taking nearly 20 years of hard fighting.

name: Vietnamese Civil War between the Mac and Trinh
Battle of Ake
description: Battle of Ake (1528), part of the Spanish Conquest of Yucatan. Spain defeated Northern Maya.

name: Battle of Damghan
description: Battle of Damghan (1528), part of the Persian-Uzbek Wars. Persia defeated Uzbekistan. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Jam
description: In 1528 the teenage Safavid Shah Tahmasp I, using artillery and a wagon-laager, defeated an Uzbek army near Jam while relieving besieged Herat, checking Shaybanid expansion into Khorasan.

name: Sack of Mombasa (1528)
description: Nuno da Cunha's second Portuguese sack of Mombasa.

name: Battle of Buda
description: Battle of Buda (1849), part of the Hungarian Revolutionary War. Habsburg Empire defeated Hungarian Rebels.

name: Battle of Florence
description: Battle of Florence (1529), part of the 2nd Habsburg-Valois War. Habsburg Empire defeated Republic of Florence.

name: Battle of Gogra
description: Battle of Gogra (1529), part of the Mughal Conquest of Northern India. Mughal Empire defeated Rajputs.

name: Battle of Landriano
description: Battle of Landriano (1529), part of the 2nd Habsburg-Valois War. Spain defeated France.

name: Battle of Shimbra Kure
description: Imam Ahmad Gragn's first decisive victory over Emperor Dawit II opened Ethiopia to Adal conquest.

name: Ethiopian-Adal War
description: 30-year conflict between Christian Ethiopia and Muslim Adal sultanate for regional dominance.

name: Inca Civil War (Huáscar vs Atahualpa)
description: Succession war between half-brothers Huáscar and Atahualpa following Huayna Capac's death. Atahualpa's victory divided and weakened the empire, critically enabling Spanish conquest within years.

name: Ottoman-Austro-Hungarian Wars
description: 170-year conflict between Ottoman and Austro-Hungarian empires.

name: Battle of Surajgarh
description: Battle of Surajgarh (1530), part of the Suri-Bengal War. Suri Empire defeated Bengal Sultanate.

name: French Expansion in Americas
description: French traders and colonists established a vast North American empire centered on the St. Lawrence River and Mississippi River systems, though ultimately defeated by the British. French colonial efforts created lasting cultural impacts in Canada and Louisiana.

name: Battle of Amba Sel
description: Gragn's victory at Amba Sel scattered the last large Ethiopian field army and led to the looting of Lalibela and Aksum.

name: Battle of Chichen Itza
description: Battle of Chichen Itza (1531), part of the Spanish Conquest of Yucatan. Maya defeated Spain.

name: Battle of Gwozdiec
description: Battle of Gwozdiec (1531), part of the Polish Moldavian War. Poland defeated Moldavia.

name: Battle of Kappel
description: Battle of Kappel (1531), part of the Swiss Religious Wars. Swiss Catholics defeated Swiss Protestants.

name: Battle of Obertyn
description: Battle of Obertyn (1531), part of the Polish Moldavian War. Poland defeated Moldavia.

name: Battle of Zug
description: Battle of Zug (1531), part of the Swiss Religious Wars. Swiss Catholics defeated Swiss Protestants.

name: Nupe Wars
description: Long arc of Nupe wars from Tsoede's foundation through Oyo invasions, internal succession wars, the Fulani jihad, and British conquest of Bida.

name: Battle of Cajamarca
description: On 16 November 1532, Francisco Pizarro's force of fewer than 200 Spaniards ambushed and captured the Inca ruler Atahualpa in the plaza of Cajamarca, slaughtering thousands of his unarmed retinue and decapitating the Inca state in a single stroke.

name: Battle of Cuzco
description: Battle of Cuzco (1532), part of the Inca War of Succession. Atahualpa defeated Huascar. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Guns
description: Battle of Guns (1532), part of the Turkish Habsburg Wars. Hungary defeated Ottoman Empire.

name: Ottoman-Safavid Wars (1532-1555)
description: Series of conflicts between Ottoman and Safavid Persian empires for control of Mesopotamia and the Caucasus, establishing dividing lines that persist today.

name: Spanish Conquest of Peru
description: Francisco Pizarro conquered the vast Inca Empire with a small force, extracting enormous wealth and establishing Spanish colonial rule. The conquest, combined with disease, devastated Andean indigenous populations.

name: Spanish Conquest of the Inca Empire
description: Francisco Pizarro's conquest of the Inca Empire, one of history's most consequential conquests, establishing Spanish colonial rule in South America.

name: Lê-Mạc Wars
description: Vietnamese civil conflict between Lê and Mạc dynasties competing for legitimacy and control, contributing to fragmentation of Vietnamese state.

name: Yaqui Wars
description: A centuries-long series of conflicts (1533-1929) in which New Spain and later the Mexican Republic repeatedly campaigned against the Yaqui of Sonora; resistance peaked in the 19th and early 20th centuries and ended only after mass deportations and a final 1920s campaign.

name: Battle of Chitor
description: Battle of Chitor (1534), part of the Mughal Conquest of Northern India. Mughal Empire defeated Gujarat.

name: Dano-Swedish Wars
description: The series of wars between Denmark and Sweden for control of the Baltic region.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Baghdad
description: Ottoman forces conquered Baghdad from the Safavids, establishing Ottoman control over Iraq for 400 years. This victory secured Ottoman dominance of Mesopotamian territory and resources.

name: Battle of Bornholm
description: Battle of Bornholm (1789), part of the 2nd Russo-Swedish War. Russia defeated Sweden.

name: Battle of Champaner
description: Battle of Champaner (1535), part of the Mughal Conquest of Northern India. Mughal Empire defeated Gujarat.

name: Battle of Mandu
description: Battle of Mandu (1535), part of the Mughal Conquest of Northern India. Mughal Empire defeated Gujarat.

name: Battle of Oksnebjerg
description: Battle of Oksnebjerg (1535), part of the Danish Counts War. Duke Christian, Sweden defeated Lubeck, Danish Catholics.

name: Toungoo–Hanthawaddy War
description: Tabinshwehti's conquest of Mon Pegu founded the First Toungoo Empire.

name: Tunis Expedition (1535)
description: Charles V's amphibious capture of Tunis and La Goletta from Hayreddin Barbarossa, restoring the Hafsid Muley Hassan as vassal.

name: Araucanian War
description: Nearly 300-year conflict between Spanish colonial forces and the Mapuche people of Chile, one of the longest indigenous resistance movements.

name: Arauco War
description: The longest indigenous resistance in the Americas. Mapuche successfully resisted Spanish conquest for 282 years, maintaining independence in southern Chile until Chilean independence.

name: Siege of Cusco
description: From May 1536 to early 1537, the Inca emperor Manco Inca Yupanqui led a massive native army in a ten-month siege of Spanish-held Cusco, seizing the fortress of Sacsayhuaman before the smaller Spanish garrison under Hernando Pizarro broke the siege; its failure cemented Spanish control of the Andes.

name: Battle of Abancay
description: Battle of Abancay (1537), part of the Civil War. Almagro Faction in Spanish Civil War defeated Pizzarists.

name: Battle of Ollantaytambo
description: Battle of Ollantaytambo (1537), part of the Spanish Conquest of Peru. Inca Rebels defeated Spain.

name: Battle of Valpovo
description: Battle of Valpovo (1537), part of the Turkish-Habsburg Wars. Ottoman Empire defeated Habsburg Empire.

name: Kaabu Empire Wars
description: Mandinka empire of Kaabu's wars from independence from Mali to its destruction at Kansala.

name: Second Venetian-Ottoman War
description: Another Ottoman victory against Venice, further establishing Ottoman naval dominance in the Mediterranean. Venice ceded more Greek territories to Ottoman control.

name: Spanish conquest of Vilcabamba
description: After the failed siege of Cusco, Manco Inca and his successors retreated to the remote jungle redoubt of Vilcabamba, sustaining an independent Neo-Inca state until 1572, when Viceroy Toledo's forces captured and executed the last Inca, Tupac Amaru.

name: Battle of Castel Nuovo
description: Battle of Castel Nuovo (1538), part of the Later Venetian-Turkish War. Ottoman Empire defeated Venice.

name: Battle of Preveza
description: On 28 September 1538 an Ottoman fleet under Hayreddin Barbarossa defeated a numerically superior Holy League fleet under Andrea Doria off Preveza. The victory, with Djerba (1560), made the Ottomans the dominant naval power in the Mediterranean for thirty years.

name: Battle of Salinas, Peru
description: Battle of Salinas, Peru (1538), part of the Spanish Civil War in Peru. Hernando Pizarro defeated Diego del Almagro.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Yemen
description: Ottoman forces conquered Yemen, establishing Ottoman control over the Red Sea and Indian Ocean approaches. Ottoman rule of Yemen lasted until the 20th century.

name: Sher Shah Sur's Campaign against Humayun
Battle of Cerquin
description: Battle of Cerquin (1539), part of the Spanish Conquest of Honduras. Spain defeated Lenca Indians. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Chausa
description: On 26 June 1539 the Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun near Chausa on the Ganges; Humayun barely escaped and Sher Shah proclaimed himself emperor.

name: Battle of Pegu
description: Battle of Pegu (1942), part of the World War II. Japan defeated United Kingdom.

name: Battle of Kannauj
description: On 17 May 1540 Sher Shah Suri again routed Humayun near Kannauj (Bilgram), driving the Mughal emperor into a fifteen-year exile and establishing Sur dynasty rule over North India.

name: Jiajing wokou raids
description: Peak of mid-16th-century 'wokou' pirate raiding (mostly Chinese, with Japanese and Portuguese crews) along China's southeast coast during the Jiajing reign, driven by Ming maritime-prohibition policy and suppressed by generals such as Qi Jiguang by 1567.

name: Mixtón War
description: Rebellion of Mixtón and neighboring peoples in northern Mexico against Spanish colonial rule. Spanish response was brutal; this conflict delayed further Spanish expansion northward.

name: Tiguex War
description: Fought in the winter of 1540-1541, the Tiguex War pitted Francisco Vazquez de Coronado's expedition and its Mexican Indian allies against the Tiwa Pueblos of the middle Rio Grande; it is considered the first named war between Europeans and Native Americans in what is now the United States, leaving hundreds of Puebloans dead.

name: Algiers Expedition (1541)
description: Charles V's disastrous amphibious expedition against Hayreddin Barbarossa's Algiers, wrecked by storm.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Budapest
description: Ottoman forces captured Budapest from Hungary, establishing Ottoman control of Central Hungary. This conquest lasted until the Great Turkish War in the late 17th century.

name: Battle of Chupas
description: Battle of Chupas (1542), part of the Spanish Civil War in Peru. Cristoval Castro defeated Diego del Almagro. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Hadden Rig
description: Battle of Hadden Rig (1542), part of the Anglo-Scottish Royal Wars. Scotland defeated England.

name: Battle of Solway Moss
description: Battle of Solway Moss (1542), part of the Anglo-Scottish Royal Wars. England defeated Scotland.

name: Battle of Wofla
description: Adal-Ottoman forces defeated and captured Cristovão da Gama, who was executed by Imam Ahmad.

name: Battle of Hjortensjon
description: Battle of Hjortensjon (1543), part of the Dacke's Rebellion. Sweden defeated Swedish Catholic Rebels. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Nice
description: Battle of Nice (1543), part of the Turkish Habsburg Wars. Ottoman Empire defeated Savoy. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Wayna Daga
description: Emperor Gelawdewos and the Portuguese survivors killed Imam Ahmad Gragn in battle, breaking Adal's invasion of Ethiopia.

name: Battle of Boulogne
description: Battle of Boulogne (1940), part of the World War II. Germany defeated France, United Kingdom.

name: Battle of Ceresole
description: Battle of Ceresole (1544), part of the 4th Habsburg-Valois War. France, Switzerland defeated Spain, Italy, German Landsknechte.

name: Battle of Serravalle
description: Battle of Serravalle (1544), part of the 4th Habsburg-Valois War. Habsburg Empire defeated Italian Mercenaries.

name: Battle of Shirts
description: Battle of Shirts (1544), part of the Scottish Clan Wars. McDonalds defeated Frasers.

name: Battle of Ancrum Moor
description: Battle of Ancrum Moor (1545), part of the Anglo-Scottish Royal Wars. Scotland defeated England.

name: Battle of Kawagoe
description: Battle of Kawagoe (1545), part of the Warring States Period in Japan. Hojo defeated Uesugi, Imagawa Ujichika and Ashikaga Haruuji.

name: Battle of Sezawa
description: Battle of Sezawa (1545), part of the Japanese Internal Conflict. Takeda Shingen defeated Ogasaware Nagatoki, Suwa Yorishige, Murakami Yoshikiyo and Kiso Yoshiyasu.

name: Battle of Spithead
description: Battle of Spithead (1545), part of the French War of Henry VIII. England defeated France.

name: Toungoo–Mrauk-U War (1545–47)
description: Tabinshwehti's failed siege of Mrauk-U.

name: Battle of Anaquito
description: Battle of Anaquito (1546), part of the Civil War. Rebels under Pizzaro defeated Spain.

name: Schmalkaldic War
description: Emperor Charles V defeated the Protestant Schmalkaldic League in a military campaign that temporarily crushed German Protestant resistance. However, the religious conflict remained unresolved and escalated after this war.

name: Battle of Drakenburg
description: Battle of Drakenburg (1547), part of the Schmalkaldic War. Schmalkaldic League defeated Habsburg Empire.

name: Battle of Huarina
description: Battle of Huarina (1547), part of the Spanish Civil War in Peru. Spanish Royalists defeated Pizzarists.

name: Battle of Muhlberg
description: Battle of Muhlberg (1547), part of the War of the German Reformation. Habsburg Empire, Saxony defeated Schmalkaldic League.

name: Battle of Pinkie
description: Battle of Pinkie (1547), part of the Anglo-Scottish Royal Wars. England defeated Scotland.

name: Burmese–Siamese War (1547–1549)
description: Tabinshwehti's siege of Ayutthaya failed, but Burma seized Upper Tenasserim.

name: Burmese–Siamese wars
description: A series of armed conflicts between the Burmese Toungoo/Konbaung empires and the Siamese Ayutthaya/Thonburi/Rattanakosin kingdoms, fought intermittently from 1547 to 1855. See per-war entries.

name: Battle of Xaquixaguana
description: Battle of Xaquixaguana (1548), part of the Spanish Civil War in Peru. Royalists defeated Pizzaro.

name: Battle of Dussindale
description: Battle of Dussindale (1549), part of the Kett's Rebellion. England defeated Norfolk Rebels. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Sampford Courtenay
description: Battle of Sampford Courtenay (1549), part of the Western Rebellion. England defeated Catholic Rebels.

name: Battle of St Marys Clyst
description: Battle of St Marys Clyst (1549), part of the Western Rebellion. England defeated Catholic Rebels.

name: Wolof Civil Wars (Battle of Danki)
description: Cayor and Baol's breakaway wars that destroyed the Jolof Empire's hegemony over Senegal.

name: Capture of Mahdia (1550)
description: Spanish-Knights of Malta capture of the Ottoman corsair base of Mahdia from Turgut Reis.

name: Chichimeca War
description: Longest and most difficult Spanish conquest-era conflict in northern Mexico. Chichimeca resistance on the Bajío frontier lasted 40 years despite superior Spanish forces.

name: Jiajing Mongol Raids
description: Altan Khan's raids on Ming borders, culminating in peace treaty.

name: Otomo-Shimazu Conflicts
description: Rival clans fighting for control of Kyushu island.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Tripoli
description: Ottoman forces conquered Tripoli from the Knights of Malta, establishing Ottoman control over North Africa. This victory secured Ottoman dominance of Mediterranean trade routes.

name: Battle of Eger
description: Battle of Eger (1552), part of the Turkish-Habsburg Wars. Habsburg Empire defeated Turkey.

name: Battle of Metz
description: Battle of Metz (1944), part of the World War II. United States defeated Germany.

name: Battle of Prome
description: Battle of Prome (1942), part of the World War II. Japan defeated United Kingdom, China.

name: Battle of Sieveshausen
description: Battle of Sieveshausen (1553), part of the War of the Germany Reformation. Saxony defeated Brandenburg.

name: Battle of Tucapel
description: Mapuche victory under Lautaro against Spanish governor Pedro de Valdivia. This battle galvanized indigenous resistance in the Arauco region.

name: Takeda-Uesugi Conflicts
description: Famous daimyo conflicts over Shinano province, including Kawanakajima battles.

name: Battle of Astrakhan
description: Battle of Astrakhan (1569), part of the Russia's Volga Wars. Russia defeated Turkey.

name: Battle of Chuquinga
description: Battle of Chuquinga (1554), part of the Spanish Civil War in Peru. Francisco Hernandez Giron defeated de Alvarado's Royalists.

name: Battle of Marciano
description: Battle of Marciano (1554), part of the 5th Habsburg-Valois Wars. Habsburg Empire defeated France.

name: Battle of Mariguenu
description: Battle of Mariguenu (1554), part of the Spanish Conquest of Chile. Araucanian Indians defeated Spain. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Oshikibata
partOf: Japan's Era of the Warring States
description: Battle of Oshikibata (1554), part of the Japan's Era of the Warring States. Mori defeated Harukata.

name: Battle of Siena
description: Battle of Siena (1554), part of the 5th Habsburg-Valois War. Habsburg Empire defeated France, Siena.

name: Battle of Temple Bar
description: Battle of Temple Bar (1554), part of the Wyatts Rebellion. England defeated Wyatt's Rebels. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Wrotham Heath
description: Battle of Wrotham Heath (1554), part of the Wyatts Rebellion. England defeated Protestant Rebels. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Havana
description: Battle of Havana (1762), part of the Seven Years War. United Kingdom defeated Spain.

name: Battle of Miyajima
partOf: Japan's Era of the Warring States
description: Battle of Miyajima (1555), part of the Japan's Era of the Warring States. Mori Motonari defeated Sue Harukata.

name: Battle of Sirhind
description: Battle of Sirhind (1710), part of the Mughal-Sikh Wars. Punjab defeated Mughal Empire. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Mori-Takeda Conflicts
description: Extended conflicts between Mori and Takeda clans for western control.

name: Ottoman-Safavid Wars in Caucasus
description: Ottoman and Safavid forces competed for control of the Caucasus, with both empires making territorial gains at different periods. The region became a contested borderland between the empires.

name: Treaty of Amasya - Ottoman-Safavid Peace
description: A peace treaty established a relatively stable border between the Ottoman and Safavid empires. The treaty established the modern border between Turkey and Iran.

name: Battle of Delhi
description: Battle of Delhi (1857), part of the Indian Mutiny. Untied Kingdom defeated Indian Rebels. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Kongo-Ndongo War of 1556
description: Defeat of Kongo forces by the Ngola of Ndongo that effectively ended Kongo's claim to suzerainty south of the Dande River.

name: Battle of Mataquito
description: Battle of Mataquito (1557), part of the Spanish Conquest of Chile. Spain defeated Araucanian Indians.

name: Battle of St Quentin
description: Battle of St Quentin (1914), part of the World War I. United Kingdom, France defeated Germany.

name: Ottoman–Ethiopian War (1557–1589)
description: Özdemir Pasha's seizure of Massawa, Arqiqo and Debarwa created the Habesh Eyalet; Sarsa Dengel finally drove the Ottomans back to the coast at Addi Qaro.

name: Battle of Calais
description: Battle of Calais (1940), part of the World War II. Germany defeated United Kingdom.

name: Battle of Gravelines
description: Battle of Gravelines (1644), part of the Thirty Years War. Netherlands, France defeated Spain.

name: Battle of Narva
description: Battle of Narva (1919), part of the Estonian War of Independence. Estonia defeated Bolsheviks.

name: Burmese–Lao War (1558–1563)
description: Bayinnaung's repeated campaigns subdued Lan Xang's Setthathirath.

name: Livonian War
description: 25-year war ending Livonian Order dominance and reshaping Baltic.

name: Battle of Hazalo
description: Emperor Gelawdewos was killed in battle against Nur ibn Mujahid of Harar at Hazalo.

name: Battle of Djerba
description: Ottoman naval forces decisively defeated a Christian coalition fleet, securing Ottoman naval supremacy in the Mediterranean. This victory prevented a Christian counter-offensive in North Africa.

name: Battle of Fellin
description: Battle of Fellin (1560), part of the Livonian War. Russia defeated Livonian Order.

name: Battle of Jamkhed
description: Battle of Jamkhed (1560), part of the Wars of the Deccan Sultanates. Bijapur, Golconda, Vijayanagar defeated Ahmadnagar.

name: Battle of Leith
description: Battle of Leith (1560), part of the Anglo-Scottish Royal Wars. Scotland, England defeated France.

name: Battle of Machiwara
description: Battle of Machiwara (1560), part of the Mughal Wars of Succession. Emperor Akbar defeated Governor Bairam Khan.

name: Battle of Okehazama
description: On 12 June 1560 Oda Nobunaga, heavily outnumbered, launched a surprise attack and killed Imagawa Yoshimoto, vaulting the Oda clan to the front rank of Sengoku warlords and launching Nobunaga's drive toward unification.

name: Battle of Oomuli
description: Battle of Oomuli (1560), part of the Livonian War. Russia defeated Livonian Order. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Kawakajima
description: Battle of Kawakajima (1561), part of the Warring States Period in Japan. Shingen defeated Uesugi.

name: Battle of Corrichie
description: Battle of Corrichie (1562), part of the Huntly Rebellion. Scotland defeated Earl of Huntly. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Dreux
description: Battle of Dreux (1870), part of the Franco-Prussian War. Prussia defeated France.

name: Battle of Hadad
description: Battle of Hadad (1562), part of the Turkish-Habsburg Wars. Ottoman Empire defeated Habsburg Empire, Transylvannia.

name: Battle of Vassy
description: Battle of Vassy (1562), part of the 1st French War of Religion.

name: Battle of Vergt
description: Battle of Vergt (1562), part of the 1st French War of Religion. French Catholics defeated French Protestants.

name: French Wars of Religion
description: A series of eight civil wars between Catholics and Protestant Huguenots devastated France for 36 years. The wars ended with the Edict of Nantes, establishing religious toleration but leaving France weakened.

name: French Wars of Religion - Huguenot Conflicts
description: Eight civil wars between Catholics and Huguenots devastated France, ending with the Edict of Nantes granting religious tolerance. The wars weakened French power and enabled other European states to rise.

name: Rajput-Mughal Wars
description: Mughal campaigns against independent Rajput kingdoms.

name: Battle of Alvsborg
description: Battle of Alvsborg (1612), part of the War of Kalmar. Denmark defeated Sweden.

name: Battle of Gotland
description: Battle of Gotland (1563), part of the Nordic Seven Years War.

name: Battle of Halmstad
description: Battle of Halmstad (1563), part of the Nordic Seven Years War. Denmark defeated Sweden.

name: Battle of Le Havre
description: Battle of Le Havre (1563), part of the 1st French War of Religion. France defeated England.

name: Battle of Mared
description: Battle of Mared (1563), part of the Nordic Seven Years War. Denmark defeated Sweden.

name: Battle of Polotsk
description: Battle of Polotsk (1579), part of the Livonian War. Poland defeated Russia.

name: Burmese–Siamese War (1563–1564)
description: War over the White Elephants forced Ayutthaya to acknowledge Toungoo overlordship.

name: Battle of Chashniki
description: Battle of Chashniki (1564), part of the Livonian War. Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth defeated Russia.

name: Battle of Coleraine
description: Battle of Coleraine (1564), part of the O'Neill Rebellion.

name: Battle of Nevel
description: Battle of Nevel (1564), part of the Livonian War. Poland defeated Russia.

name: Battle of Oland (1st)
description: Battle of Oland (1st) (1564), part of the Nordic Seven Years War. Denmark, Holy Roman Empire defeated Sweden.

name: Battle of Oland (2nd)
description: Battle of Oland (2nd) (1564), part of the Nordic Seven Years War. Sweden defeated Denmark, Holy Roman Empire.

name: Idris Alooma's Wars
description: Mai Idris Alooma's musket-equipped campaigns that restored Bornu hegemony over Kanem and the Lake Chad basin.

name: Battle of Axtorna
description: Battle of Axtorna (1565), part of the Years War Withdrawing. Denmark defeated Sweden.

name: Battle of Ballycastle
description: Battle of Ballycastle (1565), part of the O'Neill Rebellion. O'Neills defeated McDonnells.

name: Battle of Talikota
description: The Deccan sultanates' victory that ended Vijayanagara dominance and marked decline of the Hindu empire.

name: Battle of Varberg
description: Battle of Varberg (1569), part of the Nordic Seven Years War. Denmark defeated Sweden.

name: Siege of Malta (1565)
description: Ottoman siege of Malta launched from North African bases, repelled by the Knights of St. John under La Valette.

name: Spanish Conquest of the Philippines
description: Spanish forces under Miguel López de Legazpi conquered the Philippine Islands, establishing Spanish colonial rule that would last over 300 years. The conquest involved subduing Muslim sultanates and indigenous resistance movements.

name: Spanish colonization of the Philippines
description: Legazpi's expedition seized Cebu and Manila, founding Spanish rule.

name: Spanish–Moro conflict
description: 333-year intermittent warfare between Spain and the southern Muslim sultanates.

name: Battle of Gyula
description: Battle of Gyula (1566), part of the Turkish-Habsburg Wars. Ottoman Empire defeated Habsburg Empire.

name: Battle of Knockfergus
description: Battle of Knockfergus (1566), part of the O'Neill Rebellion. England defeated Tyrone.

name: Battle of Oland
description: Battle of Oland (1789), part of the 2nd Russo-Swedish War. Russia defeated Sweden.

name: Siege of Szigetvar
description: From 5 August to 8 September 1566 the Ottoman army under Suleiman the Magnificent besieged the Croatian-Hungarian fortress defended by Nikola Zrinski. Both Suleiman (of natural causes) and Zrinski died; the pyrrhic Ottoman victory halted the campaign against Vienna.

name: Battle of Carberry Hill
partOf: Uprising against Mary Queen of Scots
description: Battle of Carberry Hill (1567), part of the Uprising against Mary Queen of Scots. Rebel Scottish Lords defeated Scotland.

name: Battle of Letterkenny
description: Battle of Letterkenny (1567), part of the O'Neill Rebellion. England, O'Connells defeated O'Neills.

name: Battle of St Denis, France
description: Battle of St Denis, France (1678), part of the 3rd Dutch War. France defeated Netherlands.

name: Siege of Chittorgarh (1567-1568)
description: Akbar's Mughal army besieged the Mewar stronghold of Chittorgarh from October 1567 to February 1568; after the fort fell Akbar ordered a massacre reported at around 30,000 civilians, breaking organized Rajput resistance to the Mughals.

name: Battle of Heiligerlee
description: Battle of Heiligerlee (1568), part of the Netherlands War of Independence. Nassau defeated Friesland, Spain.

name: Battle of Jemmingen
description: Battle of Jemmingen (1568), part of the Netherlands War of Independence. Spain defeated Netherlands.

name: Battle of Jodoigne
description: Battle of Jodoigne (1568), part of the Netherlands War of Independence. Spain defeated Netherlands.

name: Battle of Langside
partOf: Uprising against Mary Queen of Scots
description: Battle of Langside (1568), part of the Uprising against Mary Queen of Scots. Regent Lord James Stewart, William Kirkaldy defeated Mary Queen of Scots, Duke of Argyll.

name: Burmese–Siamese War (1568–1569)
description: Bayinnaung's second siege captured Ayutthaya on 2 August 1569.

name: Eighty Years' War
description: 80-year conflict establishing Dutch independence from Spain.

name: Eighty Years' War - Revolt of the Netherlands
description: The Dutch Revolt against Spanish rule initiated an 80-year conflict that resulted in Dutch independence and the rise of the Dutch as a major naval and commercial power. This struggle profoundly shaped European history and colonialism.

name: Jaga Invasion of Kongo
description: Devastating invasion by the Jaga that drove King Alvaro I from Mbanza Kongo and was reversed only by a Portuguese expeditionary force under Francisco de Gouveia Sottomaior in 1574.

name: Portuguese-Mutapa War (1568-1575)
description: Francisco Barreto's failed Portuguese expedition up the Zambezi to seize the gold mines of Mutapa, recounted by Beach and Newitt as the opening Portuguese intervention.

name: Siege of Malacca (1568)
description: Sultan Alauddin al-Kahar's failed Acehnese siege of Portuguese Malacca.

name: Ayutthaya-Toungoo Conflicts
description: Burma captured and sacked Ayutthaya, Siam's capital, but failed to maintain control.

name: Battle of Jarnac
description: Battle of Jarnac (1569), part of the 3rd French War of Religion. French Catholics defeated Hugenots.

name: Battle of La Roche-LAbeille
description: Battle of La Roche-LAbeille (1569), part of the 3rd French War of Religion. French Protestants, German Protestants defeated French Catholics.

name: Battle of Moncontour
description: Battle of Moncontour (1569), part of the 3rd French War of Religion. French Catholics, Spain, Italy, Switzerland defeated French Protestants.

name: Battle of Orthez
description: Battle of Orthez (1814), part of the Napoleonic Wars. United Kingdom, Portugal defeated France.

name: Azai-Oda Conflicts
description: Oda Nobunaga's campaign against Azai clan.

name: Battle of Anegawa
description: Battle of Anegawa (1570), part of the Japan's Warring States Period. Oda Nobunaga, Tokugawa Ieyasu defeated Asakura Yoshikage, Asai Nagamasa.

name: Battle of Arnay-le-Duc
description: Battle of Arnay-le-Duc (1570), part of the French War . French Protestants defeated French Catholics.

name: Battle of Famagusta
description: Battle of Famagusta (1570), part of the Venetian-Turkish War in Cyprus. Ottoman Empire defeated Venice. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Gelt
description: Battle of Gelt (1570), part of the Dacres Rebellion. England defeated Anglo-Scottish Borderers.

name: Battle of Ishiyama Honganji
partOf: Japan's Era of the Warring States
description: Battle of Ishiyama Honganji (1570), part of the Japan's Era of the Warring States. Oda Nobunaga defeated Ikko Sect.

name: Cyprus War (Ottoman-Venetian)
description: Ottoman conquest of Cyprus from Venice, establishing Ottoman control of eastern Mediterranean.

name: Kano–Katsina Wars
description: Two centuries of intermittent war between the rival Hausa city-states of Kano and Katsina over trade routes and tribute.

name: Ottoman Conquest of Cyprus
description: Ottoman forces conquered Cyprus from Venice despite Christian naval victory at Lepanto, establishing Ottoman control of the eastern Mediterranean. Cyprus remained Ottoman for over 300 years.

name: Third Venetian-Ottoman War
description: Ottoman forces conquered Cyprus from Venice, though the Holy League achieved a naval victory at Lepanto. Despite Lepanto, Ottoman naval power recovered and Venice had to cede Cyprus.

name: Battle of Craibstane
description: Battle of Craibstane (1571), part of the Huntly Rebellion. Scotland defeated Catholic Rebels.

name: Battle of Enryakuji
description: Battle of Enryakuji (1571). Oda Nobunaga defeated Enryakuji Buddhist Monks.

name: Battle of Lepanto
description: The Holy League Christian fleet achieved a decisive naval victory against the Ottoman Navy, though it was not strategically conclusive. This battle became symbolic of Christian resistance to Ottoman expansion despite Ottoman recovery afterward.

name: Battle of Tillyangus
description: Battle of Tillyangus (1571), part of the Huntly Rebellion. Huntlys defeated Clan Gordon.

name: Battle of Ahmadabad
description: Battle of Ahmadabad (1780), part of the 1st British-Maratha War. United Kingdom defeated Marathas.

name: Battle of Brielle
description: Battle of Brielle (1572), part of the y Netherlands War of Independence . Netherlands defeated Spain.

name: Battle of Goes
description: Battle of Goes (1572), part of the Netherlands War of Independence. Spain defeated Netherlands.

name: Battle of Haarlem
description: Battle of Haarlem (1572), part of the Netherlands War of Independence. Spain defeated Netherlands. Battle followed by a massacre.

name: Battle of Havre
description: Battle of Havre (1572), part of the Netherlands War of Independence. Spain defeated French Hugenouts.

name: Battle of Huayna Pucara
description: Battle of Huayna Pucara (1572), part of the Tupac Amaru Revolt. Spain defeated Inca Rebels.

name: Battle of Massapa
description: Engagement during the Barreto expedition against the Mongas, fought near the Portuguese feira of Massapa on the Mutapa frontier.

name: Battle of Mikata ga hara
partOf: Japan's Era of the Warring States
description: Battle of Mikata ga hara (1572), part of the Japan's Era of the Warring States. Shingen defeated Ieyasu.
